predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: Chlothar I's share of Clovis I's kingdom at the partition, centred on Soissons

successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: what was left of Neustria in 613: the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen, now the core of Chlothar II's reunited realm

ledger.x: 511: At Clovis I's death his four sons partition the Frankish kingdom and Chlothar I takes Soissons.
524: On Chlodomer's death 'Chlothar I received Touraine and Poitou' (Chlodomer page); Childebert I took the Loire territories with Orléans.
558: Childebert I dies and Chlothar I reunites the realm.
561: Chlothar I dies and Chilperic I receives Soissons, 'the smallest kingdom'.

567: 'On the death of Charibert in 567, Chilperic's estates were augmented when the brothers divided Charibert's kingdom among themselves and agreed to share Paris and the territory around it' (Chilperic I page).
575: After Sigebert I's murder Chilperic I seizes Tours and Poitiers from Austrasia, 'along with places in Aquitaine such as Saintes and territory in Auvergne'.

578: 'In 578, the Frankish king Chilperic I sent an army to fight Waroch along the Vilaine'; after three days Waroch 'did homage for Vannes, sent his son as a hostage, and agreed to pay an annual tribute' (Waroch II page; the Chilperic I page calls Chilperic's dominion over the Bretons 'relatively secure').

584: After Chilperic's death 'Two envoys from Brunhilde ... succeeded in swaying Limoges, Tours, and Poitiers'; Guntram's troops recovered them and they returned to Guntram and Clothar (undated on the page).
587: 'In 587, he [Guntram] managed to capture the towns of Angers, Saintes, and Nantes' (Chlothar II page).
596: 'In 596, Clotaire and Fredegund took Paris, which was supposed to be held in common.'

599: Theuderic II and Theudebert II defeat Chlothar II at Dormelles, 'forcing him to sign a treaty that reduced his kingdom to the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen'; the rest was split between the two brothers.

599: The northern cities of Chilperic's 561 share (Soissons, Arras, Cambrai, Thérouanne, Tournai, Boulogne) are read as Theudebert II's part of the remainder 'split between' the two brothers; the page does not say who took which land (confidence 1).
613: Theuderic II dies at Metz and 'the entire realm was delivered into Chlothar's hands'; Chlothar II becomes 'the sole royal ruler of the Frankish peoples'.

wars.name: Wars of Chilperic I and Sigebert I
wars.outcome: Sigebert defeated Chilperic after the 567 division, retook Reims and 'seized Soissons'; Chilperic allied with Guntram in 573 but 'again lost the war'; after Sigebert's murder in 575 Chilperic took Tours, Poitiers and Saintes.

wars.name: Chilperic I's campaign against Waroch II
wars.outcome: Waroch II did homage for Vannes but broke his oath later; Chilperic's dominion over the Bretons was 'relatively secure'.

wars.name: Wars of Chlothar II against Theudebert II and Theuderic II
wars.outcome: Chlothar and Fredegund took Paris in 596 and the Austrasian and Burgundian armies were beaten at Laffaux; at Dormelles in 599 Chlothar was defeated and his kingdom reduced to Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen.

wars.name: Chlothar II's reunification of the Franks
wars.outcome: On Theuderic II's death at Metz in late 613 the whole realm was delivered to Chlothar II, who executed Brunhilda; the Edict of Paris followed in 614.

certainty.note: Partitions are given by cities, not frontiers, and the 561 outline is the departments of six named cities; the lines of 524, 567, 575, 587 and 599 are cities and regions, never boundaries.
